{{Quote|I just like antiques. I've got a proper ''beskad'', too.|[[Goran Beviin]]|<ref name="APM">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref>}}
A '''''beskad''''' was a traditional [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Sword/Legends|saber]], primarily forged from nearly indestructible [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]]. Comprised of a single-edged blade with a [[Leather/Legends|leather]]-bound hilt, the ''beskad'' was a weighty and incredibly resilient weapon, capable of delivering powerful blows with each swing. Designed to batter down an enemy's defenses, ''beskade'' were a favored weapon of the ancient Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], though the use of the heavy iron blade spanned millennia.

==Description==
Based on the design of ancient [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] sabers, ''beskade'' were traditionally single-edged, curved [[Sword/Legends|swords]]<ref name="TBHC" /> that tapered upward to a sharp point, featuring a hilt with a protective crossguard and pommel. Typically possessed of a flat blade, forty-five [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] in length and between five and six centimeters in width, a ''beskad'' weighed approximately two [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] or more in total. ''Beskade'' could be made of [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]], but were more commonly forged from Mandalorian [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]],<ref name="Revelation" /> a nearly indestructible [[Ore/Legends|ore]]<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> found only on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and its [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]],<ref name="NewBattlefronts">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> both located at the heart of [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian space]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> During the creation of a ''beskad'', the metal used to forge the blade would be heated until it glowed [[Color/Legends|red]]-hot, and shaped into a workable bar. A [[metalsmith]] would then strike and repeatedly fold the metal—traditionally with a [[Hammer (tool)/Legends|hammer]] and tongs—layering the material again and again for increased strength, before finally cooling the finished blade in liquid; the rough sword edge would later be honed to a razor sharpness, and the hilt bound in [[Leather/Legends|leather]].<ref name="Revelation" />

Due to the weight and overall shape of a ''beskad'', wielding the Mandalorian saber traditionally required a single-handed grip. Those unfamiliar with the weapon were known to compare the ''beskad'' to an [[Farm/Legends|agricultural]] or undergrowth clearing tool,<ref name="Revelation" /> such as a [[Machete/Legends|machete]],<ref name="CoPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> or a well-balanced warhammer.<ref name="Revelation" /> Accordingly, ''beskade'' were often used to batter through enemies' defenses<ref name="TBHC" /> by using the heftiness of the blade to overcome an opponent. The traditional Mandalorian style of fighting with a ''beskad'' capitalized on the full body protection offered by a [[Soldier/Legends|warrior's]] [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|armor]] to move in close to an enemy without fear of injury, often inside their reach in order to deprive them of maneuverability or the ability to parry, and subsequently hammer away at them.<ref name="Revelation" /> A heavy swing from a ''beskad'' was capable of embedding the blade in both [[Armor/Legends|armor]]<ref name="APM" /> and [[Bone/Legends|bone]], and a ''beskar''-forged saber was even capable of stopping a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="Revelation" />

==History==
{{Quote|Look, if Vau felt you lacked the killer edge, he'd crank it up a little. He'd make you fight your brother. We had a choice. We could fight each other until one was too badly hurt to stand up, or we could fight ''him''."<br />"And?''"<br />"''I opted to take on Vau. He had a real ''Mando'' iron saber, and I was unarmed. I just went at him. I never wanted to kill so badly in my life and he just cut me up.|[[Clone commando/Legends|Republic Commandos]] [[Atin Skirata|Atin]] and [[Fi Skirata]]|<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref>}}
The ancient Taung, the progenitors of the Mandalorian culture, were a [[Mandalorian religion|religiously]] zealous people who viewed close-quarters combat as a warrior's highest calling. In battle, they relied heavily on ''beskade'', usually wielded in combination with a [[Kal/Legends|''kal'']] [[Knife/Legends|dagger]] in their off [[Limb/Legends|hand]]. The legacy of the ancient warriors' use of ''beskade'' and ''kale'' led to Mandalorian armor pieces worn on a soldier's right side to be referred to as the ''beskad'' plates, counter to the left-side plates which were referred to as the ''kal'' plates.<ref name="TBHC" />

[[File:Beskad_the_Warrior.jpg|thumb|left|The ex-Mandalorian warrior known as "[[Beskad (Mandalorian)|Beskad]]," wielding the namesake blade]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Mandalorian warrior [[Jicoln Cadera]] owned a [[Jicoln Cadera's beskad|''beskad'']]. Cadera's saber differed significantly from the norm, being possessed of three blades arranged in a triangular formation, with a crossguard adorned with [[Tooth/Legends|fanged]] skulls meant to represent felled warriors, and a pommel in the shape of a sculpted [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt dragon]], symbolizing the hunger for war and destruction prized by Mandalorians of the era.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Years later, an ex-Mandalorian member of the [[Dar'manda]] group went by the name of "[[Beskad (Mandalorian)|Beskad]]," and wielded one of the namesake sabers in combat.<ref name="Onslaught">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught]]''</ref>

Millennia later, the Mandalorian soldier [[Walon Vau]] came into possession of a ''beskad''. Shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|opening battle]] of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Vau made use of his ''beskad'' in a duel with one of the Republic's [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] whom he had trained prior to the war's outbreak. In an effort to emotionally harden the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] soldier—known by the nickname of [[Atin Skirata|Atin]]—in the wake of his recently developed survivor's guilt, Vau fought and eventually severely wounded the other man with his ''beskad'', leaving a number of scars.<ref name="TZ" /> In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], another [[Commando/Legends|commando]] who had trained under Vau, [[Sev/Legends|Sev]] of [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]], jokingly mused about getting a ''beskad'' of his own.<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>

By the year [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], the veteran Mandalorian soldier [[Goran Beviin]] owned an ancient ''beskad'', considered by that time to be an antique. When confronted for his possession of a pair of illegal Mandalorian [[Crushgaunt/Legends|crushgaunts]] by his contemporary, [[Briika Jeban]], Beviin insisted that he enjoyed both his crushgaunts and ''beskad'' for their antiquarian value. However, during a confrontation on [[New Holgha]] in the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Beviin used his ''beskad'' in [[Battle of New Holgha|combat]] with a [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[subaltern]], ultimately killing the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] invader with his crushgaunts.<ref name="APM" /> Beviin continued to carry the ''beskar'' iron saber for years after, killing a number of Yuuzhan Vong warriors with the blade outside of [[Bralsin]], during their [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attack]] on Mandalore.<ref name="Revelation" /> Beviin's husband, [[Medrit Vasur]], was a skilled Mandalorian metalsmith, capable of forging tempered ''beskade'' from raw ''beskar'' in his workshop on their [[Clan Beviin|family's]] [[Beviin-Vasur farm|farm]].<ref name="Sacrifice" /> In [[41 ABY]], Beviin taught [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] to use a ''beskad'' during the course of her training on Mandalore in alternate combat techniques.<ref name="Revelation" /> Solo later put this training to use in [[Second Battle of Roche|battle]] against her [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] brother, [[Darth Caedus]], using a ''beskad'' to [[Cho mok/Legends|remove]] one of his arms.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
An iron Mandalorian saber was first mentioned in the novel ''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]'', written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[February 28]], [[2006]].<ref name="TZ" /> Later that same year, Traviss introduced the saber fully in her [[EBook|e-novella]] ''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]'', providing the ''beskad'' name as well as a general appearance for the weapon.<ref name="APM" /> A ''beskad'' was later mentioned in Traviss' subsequent entry in the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novel series, [[Republic Commando: True Colors|''True Colors'']],<ref name="TC" /> and the weapon appeared again in two of Traviss' contributions to the multi-author ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' series, [[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice|''Sacrifice'']]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and [[Legacy of the Force: Revelation|''Revelation'']],<ref name="Revelation" /> as well as [[Troy Denning]]'s conclusion to the series, [[Legacy of the Force: Invincible|''Invincible'']].<ref name="Invincible" />
